author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Sen. Mitch McConnell returned to Capitol Hill Monday after a three-month absence linked to health problems, according to CNN reporting carried by WHDH.

The Kentucky Republican was seen leaving his home in a wheelchair and said he planned to cast his first Senate vote since a June fall. He also said he was continuing physical therapy and was not yet fully recovered.

McConnell was hospitalized June 14. Weeks later, he disclosed that he had fallen, briefly lost consciousness and later contracted pneumonia. He then continued his recovery at home after a period in rehabilitation.

The Senate returned to session Monday after a five-week summer recess, putting McConnell back in the chamber as lawmakers resumed work. His long absence had prompted public questions about his health and ability to serve.

McConnell has said he will not seek reelection in 2026 and intends to finish his term, which is scheduled to end in January. He remains a Republican senator from Kentucky and a former Senate majority leader.
dek: The Kentucky Republican said he would cast his first Senate vote since a June fall as he continues physical therapy.
headline: Mitch McConnell returns to Senate after three-month health-related absence
